articles.title: Baseline [68Ga]Ga-DOTANOC PET quantification for outcome prediction in patients with neuroendocrine tumours treated with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE PRRT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is an established therapeutic option for advanced somatostatin-receptor-expressing neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) patients. However, reproducible PET-derived biomarkers to stratify patients before treatment remain incompletely defined. This study evaluated whether pre-PRRT PET-derived parameters were associated with outcome. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included NET patients studied with baseline [68Ga]Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT before [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE PRRT. Candidate PET-variables included whole-body and site-specific MITV (molecular imaging tumour volume), MITV*SUVmean, MITV-to-SUVmean ratios. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates, univariable Cox-regression, LASSO-Cox regression for variable selection, and final multivariable Cox models. RESULTS: Forty-one patients were included; at a median follow-up of 42.6 months (95%CI, 39.9-62.1), 25 PFS events and 10 deaths occurred. Median-PFS was 35.6 months (95% CI, 26.2 months to not reached), whereas median-OS was not reached. In the final multivariable PFS model, TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio remained independently associated with PFS (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.003-1.085; p = 0.032), whereas NodesMITV did not reach statistical significance. In the multivariable OS model, TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; p = 0.024) and Ki67 (HR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.05-1.37; p = 0.007) were associated with OS, whereas surgery of the primary tumour was not. Patients with a TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio above the cohort median had shorter median-PFS (26.2 vs. 38.1 months). CONCLUSION: Pre-PRRT [68Ga]Ga-DOTANOC TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio was independently associated with PFS and showed a supportive association with OS. This composite parameter, capturing the relationship between SSTR-PET-defined tumour burden and mean tracer uptake intensity, warrants external validation.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Prognostic value of right ventricular function derived from 13N-ammonia PET in patients with ischemic heart disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) and right ventricular (RV) fractional area change (FAC) assessed by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) are associated with cardiovascular events; however, data on RV function derived from myocardial PET remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether TAPSE and FAC measured using 13N-ammonia PET (NH3-PET) correlate with TTE measurements and predict major adverse cardiac events (MACEs) in patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD). METHODS: This retrospective study included patients who underwent both NH3-PET and TTE with TAPSE and FAC measurements between 2015 and 2021. Patients who underwent NH3-PET alone during the same period were randomly assigned to the main and validation cohorts. The endpoint was MACE, defined as cardiac death and hospitalisation for heart failure. Optimal cutoff values for PET-TAPSE and PET-FAC were determined using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and prognostic performance was validated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The study comprised 200 patients who were followed up for 40 ± 23 months. PET-TAPSE and PET-FAC correlated significantly with TTE measurements (TAPSE: r = 0.84, p < 0.0001; FAC: r = 0.41, p = 0.033). Patients with reduced PET-TAPSE or PET-FAC had significantly higher MACE rates than those with preserved values (both p < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified PET-FAC as an independent predictor of MACE in imaging-based and clinically adjusted models (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.95; HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.79-0.93). CONCLUSION: RV function derived from NH3-PET correlates with TTE measurements and contributes to MACE risk stratification in patients with IHD.

articles.title: Axonal signal fraction imaging from diffusion MRI.
articles.abstract: Axonal loss is a hallmark of a wide range of brain diseases and has motivated the development of diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) methods for estimating the axonal signal fraction (ASF), a quantity proportional to the axonal volume fraction within a voxel. Most existing approaches rely on multi-compartment models of the dMRI signal, introducing several assumptions, particularly regarding extra-axonal diffusion. Alternative methods can avoid these assumptions but require specialized acquisition schemes that are not widely available in clinical practice. We present a dMRI framework for estimating ASF without explicitly modeling extra-axonal diffusion, while remaining compatible with clinically available pulsed gradient spin-echo (PGSE) acquisitions and thus avoiding the need for advanced diffusion encodings. ASF imaging uses a machine-learning regressor informed by a biophysical model that relates axonal diffusivities and ASF to the spherical harmonic representation of two high-b-value shells. We assess the robustness of the estimated ASF and axonal diffusivities, evaluate their accuracy using Monte Carlo simulations, and investigate their behavior in the presence of membrane permeability. Across both clinical data and data acquired on a high-performance Connectome MRI system, ASF maps exhibit qualitatively consistent contrast and spatial patterns resembling those observed in a post-mortem myelin-stained human brain atlas. These findings suggest that ASF imaging can provide robust estimates of the axonal signal fraction without explicit modeling of extra-axonal diffusion, while remaining compatible with current clinical acquisition protocols.

articles.title: Confidence-Aware Mixup for Universal Semi-Supervised Medical Image Classification.
articles.abstract: In medical image classification, the unlabeled images available for semi-supervised learning (SSL) often include classes or imaging domains that are absent from the labeled set. Existing universal SSL methods usually add modules that detect those out-of-distribution (OOD) samples, such as prototype-based gates or open-set heads, which introduce extra hyperparameters and can be unstable with few labeled images. We propose Confidence-Aware Mixup (CAM), which relies on the classifier's own confidence without adding any OOD detector or other auxiliary module. For each unlabeled image, CAM keeps the predicted-class probability, spreads the remaining probability evenly over the other classes, and mixes this target with a labeled image through MixUp. We compared CAM with 14 published SSL methods on dermatology, ophthalmology, and chest radiography benchmarks. With fixed hyperparameters for every method, CAM achieved the highest balanced accuracy in 10 of 12 single-label settings and the highest aggregate balanced accuracy on both single-label benchmarks. In the multi-label CheXpert setting, it achieved the highest mean AUC and mAP with 100 labeled patients. Code for this work is available at https://github.com/PyJulie/CAM.

articles.title: Evaluating the performance of Large Language Models in answering questions from Italian medical e-learning courses and potential ethical concerns: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: This study conducts a controlled evaluation of four freely accessible Large Language Models-ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and DeepSeek-by testing their ability to answer questions from Italian Continuing Medical Education (CME) courses, with attention to accuracy, consistency across domains, and associated ethical concerns. A total of 47 CME courses were selected, and their multiple-choice questionnaires were submitted to the LLMs. A passing threshold of 75% was used to define successful course completion. Performance was assessed based on pass rates and the percentage of correct answers. DeepSeek scored the highest (87%), followed by ChatGPT (85%), Gemini (83%), and Perplexity (81%). LLMs performed more reliably on generalist courses than on highly specialized ones. Despite promising results, limitations include the absence of a deep statistical analysis, lack of a control group, and technical constraints with some models. Ethical concerns and risks such as hallucinations and misinformation require cautious use and human oversight. Responsible integration of LLMs into medical education requires clear standards and coordination among AI developers, educators, clinicians, legislators, and academic authorities.

articles.title: Relative tracer delivery from [18F]MK6240 PET imaging as a perfusion-sensitive biomarker across aging and clinically defined cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Recent studies indicate that dynamic [18F]MK6240 PET can provide information on cerebral perfusion in addition to tau pathology. This study evaluates [18F]MK6240 relative tracer delivery R1 as a surrogate for perfusion across aging and clinical stages of cognitive impairment and examines its associations with demographic variables, regional brain volume, Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology and cognitive performance. METHODS: A total of 116 participants, including cognitively unimpaired (CU) individuals and those with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD, underwent dynamic [18F]MK6240 and [11C]PiB PET, and structural MRI. AD-specific regions of interest (ROIs) were used to quantify R1 (cerebral perfusion), [18F]MK6240 distribution volume ratio DVR (tau pathology), and [11C]PiB DVR (amyloid-beta Aβ). Associations between R1 and demographic factors, ROI volume, AD pathology, and cognitive function were evaluated. Additional analyses examined R1 across tau PET staging regions, and secondary analyses explored effects within clinical and Aβ status subgroups. Multiple comparisons were corrected using the false discovery rate (FDR) and results were reported as q-values. RESULTS: R1 values exhibited a distinct regional rank order that followed the anatomical sequence of typical AD tau progression. In the full cohort, older age was associated with lower regional R1 (Spearman's |rs|= 0.237-0.360, q = 0.022-0.001) and remained significant after adjustment for tau and Aβ burdens. Minimal associations were observed between R1 and ROI volumes, suggesting that regional R1 variability was not driven by cortical atrophy. Associations between R1 and global or regional Aβ burden were not significant after FDR correction. In contrast, moderate negative associations were observed between regional R1 and tau burden (|rs| = 0.247-0.421, q = 0.0003-0.043). Better global cognition was associated with higher R1 (|rs| = 0.243-0.252, q = 0.043), although associations were attenuated after age adjustment. Secondary subgroup analyses suggested disease stage-dependent effects, with stronger R1-tau and R1-volume associations in symptomatic participants and stronger R1-age, and R1-Aβ associations in CU Aβ⁻ individuals. CONCLUSION: These findings highlight age, tau burden and cognition as key correlates of cerebral perfusion, while supporting [18F]MK6240 R1 as a complementary marker of brain function.

articles.title: Richardson-type metabolic pattern predicts clinical progression in progressive supranuclear palsy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP)-related metabolic patterns on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) can aid diagnosis of PSP. Given that many PSP variants evolve toward the prototypic PSP-Richardson's syndrome (PSP-RS) phenotype during disease progression, a PSP-RS-related pattern (richardsonPSPRP) may capture an essential disease signature. We evaluated whether expression of a richardsonPSPRP reflects disease severity and longitudinal clinical progression in prospective Korean PSP cohorts. METHODS: We derived Korean richardsonPSPRP from probable PSP-RS (n = 20) and HC (n = 24) with external validation in a Taiwanese PSP-RS cohort (n = 32). We estimated individual richardsonPSPRP expression z-scores in 81 patients with PSP (55 PSP-RS and 26 variants) and 77 with PD. The diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of richardsonPSPRP z-score were investigated with clinical measures both cross-sectionally and longitudinally using correlation analyses and linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: The richardsonPSPRP excellently discriminated PSP-RS from HC in the derivation and Taiwanese validation cohorts (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] = 0.99 for both) and differentiated PSP from PD (AUROC = 0.90). Higher richardsonPSPRP expression correlated with greater disease severity (PSP rating scale: r = 0.61; PSP clinical deficits scale: r = 0.47), poorer cognition (Mini-Mental State Examination: r=-0.56; Montreal Cognitive Assessment: r=-0.54) and activities of daily living (r=-0.62). Higher baseline richardsonPSPRP z-score predicted faster longitudinal progression on the PSP rating scale (β = 0.25, P = 0.0028) and PSP clinical deficits scale (β = 0.062, P = 0.0038) in overall and variant PSP cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: The richardsonPSPRP expression may be useful for assessing disease burden across the PSP spectrum, warranting validation in large multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Test-retest repeatability of deep learning-enabled quantitative PET parameters and PROMISE criteria-based lesion index in 18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET/CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: PSMA-targeted PET/CT (PSMA-PET/CT) is increasingly used for prostate cancer staging, selection of patients for PSMA-directed radioligand therapy, and longitudinal assessment of treatment response. Multiple quantitative frameworks, including the Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) criteria, have been proposed to standardize interpretation, yet limited studies have established the test-retest repeatability and reliability of quantitative PSMA-PET measures, which is a prerequisite before any parameter can be used to define treatment eligibility or to distinguish true response from progression. We evaluated the repeatability of deep learning-enabled lesion-level SUV-based and volume-dominated features, together with the PROMISE-criteria-based lesion index (LI), to provide repeatability benchmarks for future studies of response assessment and treatment selection. METHODS: Twenty-two men with metastatic prostate cancer underwent two 18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET/CT scans 1 to 7 days apart with no intervening therapy. Lesions were detected, segmented, localized to PROMISE anatomic regions, and quantified using the FDA-cleared and deep learning-enabled aPROMISE platform; false-positive detections were manually removed, and lesions were matched one-to-one between scans. After excluding two patients without matched lesions, 20 patients with 292 matched lesion pairs were analyzed. SUVmax, SUVmean, SUVpeak, SUVtotal, lesion volume, and LI were assessed. Repeatability was quantified using the within-subject coefficient of variation (wCOV), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC(2,1)), and log-scale Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement (LOA), with volume-threshold, lesion-site, and scan-interval sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Among the SUV-based features, SUVmean was the most repeatable (wCOV = 7.04%, ICC(2,1) = 0.984, 95% LOA = - 17.1% to 22.7%), while the volume-dominated features SUVtotal and lesion volume showed greater variability (wCOV = 24.92% and 24.53%, respectively). LI demonstrated the highest repeatability of all evaluated measures (wCOV = 3.88%, ICC(2,1) = 0.986, 95% LOA = - 9.4% to 12.2%). Volume thresholding generally narrowed the limits of agreement and reduced variability, and the relative ordering of feature repeatability was largely preserved across scan intervals. CONCLUSIONS: SUVmean was the most repeatable SUV-based feature, supporting its further prospective evaluation for lesion-level response and progression assessment, whereas PROMISE criteria-based LI demonstrated the highest repeatability overall, supporting further evaluation as a standardized measure of PSMA expression and potential quantitative imaging biomarker, including for treatment-eligibility decisions. By establishing the test-retest repeatability of these measures, this study provides repeatability benchmarks for quantitative 18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET/CT features and supports their further evaluation as imaging biomarkers in prostate cancer.

articles.title: Interaction effects of nucleus basalis of Meynert atrophy and glymphatic dysfunction with tau deposition across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: a multimodal PET/MR study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM) degeneration and glymphatic dysfunction act independently or interactively associated with medial temporal tau vulnerability and cognitive impairment across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 114 participants, including 23 amyloid-negative normal controls (NC), 55 amyloid-positive individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 36 amyloid-positive patients with AD, underwent amyloid (Aβ) PET/CT and tau PET/MR scans. Glymphatic function was quantified with diffusion tensor imaging along perivascular spaces (DTI-ALPS) index and centrum semiovale perivascular space volume fraction (PVSVF-CSO). A perivascular imaging composite (PIC), derived from the reverse-coded ALPS index and PVSVF-CSO, was further used to evaluate its interaction effects with normalized NBM volume on medial temporal tau burden. Elastic net regression was used to examine multimodal prediction of cognitive performance. RESULTS: Normalized NBM volume and ALPS index progressively decreased across the AD continuum (all P < 0.05), PVSVF-CSO was higher in the MCI and AD groups than in the NC group (adjusted P = 0.005 and 0.003, respectively). In the combined symptomatic cohort, smaller normalized NBM volume and lower ALPS index were associated with higher selected medial temporal regions tau burden and worse cognitive performance (all P < 0.05). Parahippocampal gyrus (PHG) tau partially mediated the association between normalized NBM volume and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score (indirect effect: β = 17.25, 95% CI [0.52, 34.04], accounted for 27.9% of the total effect). Normalized NBM volume and its interaction with PIC were significantly associated with PHG tau burden (β = - 0.394, P < 0.001; β = - 0.166, P = 0.042). The exploratory elastic net model modestly predicted MoCA score (R2 = 0.105). CONCLUSIONS: Cholinergic degeneration and glymphatic dysfunction are interrelated processes that show an interactive association with selected medial temporal tau vulnerability. PHG tau partially mediates the association between normalized NBM volume and cognitive performance.

articles.title: Plaque inflammation and noncalcified burden at treated lesions associated with outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess whether pre-procedural coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-derived plaque parameters reflecting inflammation and component at lesions treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were associated with future risk. MATERIALS & METHODS: Patients with chronic coronary syndrome who underwent CCTA followed by PCI within 30 days were included across three tertiary centers in 2021-2022. Pre-PCI pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation (PCAT attenuation, a marker of local coronary inflammation) and plaque components (calcified, noncalcified, low-attenuation) were quantified from CCTA at PCI-treated lesions. The primary endpoint was the composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, repeat revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. Exploratory mediation analysis evaluated periprocedural myocardial infarction (PMI) as a potential mediator. RESULTS: Among 2013 patients included, 226 (11.2%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 2.5 years. Higher PCAT attenuation (adjusted HR per SD: 1.53; 95% CI: 1.34-1.74; p < 0.001) and greater noncalcified burden (adjusted HR per SD: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.04-1.36; p = 0.012) were independently associated with increased MACE risk after PCI. The prognostic effect of PCAT attenuation was stronger in patients with hyperlipidemia (p for interaction = 0.006). PMI mediated 1.7% (95% CI: 0.2-4.4%) and 4.5% (95% CI: 0.3-17.6%) of the associations of PCAT attenuation and noncalcified burden with MACE, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Plaque inflammation and noncalcified burden are associated with prognosis after PCI. These findings support the potential utility of these markers in guiding future investigations of treatment strategies. KEY POINTS: Question Plaque features at PCI-treated lesions may influence prognosis, but their value for post-procedural risk stratification remains insufficiently defined. Findings In 2013 patients, higher pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation and noncalcified plaque burden at treated lesions were independently associated with adverse cardiovascular events. Clinical relevance Pre-procedural CCTA assessment of inflammation and noncalcified burden at treated lesions may help identify patients at increased risk after PCI and support individualized management.

articles.title: Bleomycin electroembolotherapy (BEET) for arteriovenous malformations: outcomes in a prospective bicentric study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This prospective study aims to evaluate the safety and clinical outcomes of bleomycin electroembolotherapy (BEET) for treating extracranial arteriovenous malformations (AVMs). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This represents a subanalysis of the prospective multicenter APOLLON trial (Clinical trial register, DRKS00021019). Children and adults with symptomatic AVMs unsuitable for or refractory to conventional treatments underwent BEET at two specialized vascular anomaly centers. Clinical and imaging findings were assessed at baseline and at 6-month follow-up intervals to evaluate subjective outcome (symptom-free, partial relief, no improvement, clinical progression) and AVM lesion devascularization on MRI (total, 100%; substantial, 76-99%; partial, 51-75%; slight, 50%; progression). Minor and major complications were assessed according to the CIRSE classification system. RESULTS: Thirty-eight patients with symptomatic AVMs, mostly of fine-fistulous type (Cho IIIa, 25/38, 65.8%) and located in the face (20/38, 52.6%), lower (12/38, 31.6%) or upper extremities (6/38, 15.8%), underwent 84 procedures. The mean number of procedures per patient was 2.2 ± 1.5. Mean dose of the bleomycin was 8.3 ± 5.0 mg per session. Twenty-eight patients (73.7%) showed partial relief of symptoms, 9/38 (23.7%) patients were symptom-free, and 1/38 (2.6%) showed no improvement of symptoms. MRI was available in 34/38 (89.5%) patients. Substantial devascularization (76-99%) was assessed in 18/34 (52.9%), partial devascularization (51-75%) in 10/34 (29.4%), and complete devascularization in 4/34 (11.8%) patients, while slight devascularization was achieved in 2/34 (5.9%) patients. There was one major complication, a post-therapeutic ulceration of the lip managed with debridement and defect reconstruction (1/84, 1.2%; grade 3). CONCLUSION: BEET demonstrated promising short-term clinical and imaging results, with a low rate of major complications. Notably, favorable outcomes were observed in predominantly complex cases, such as fine-fistulous lesions and challenging locations like the face and distal extremities. KEY POINTS: Question Current treatment of extracranial arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) remains challenging, particularly in therapy-refractory and difficult-to-treat lesions, requiring effective minimally invasive alternatives. Findings Bleomycin electroembolotherapy (BEET) achieved symptom improvement in 97.4% of patients with AVMs in the face or distal extremities, substantial/complete devascularization in 64.7%, with one major complication. Clinical relevance BEET represents a promising minimally invasive treatment option for AVMs, providing meaningful symptom relief and lesion devascularization with an acceptable safety profile, including challenging fine-fistulous lesions and anatomically difficult regions.

articles.title: AI-integrated versus Standard Mammography Screening Pathways: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
articles.abstract: Purpose To compare the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated and standard mammography screening pathways for breast cancer detection using Bayesian network meta-analysis. Materials and Methods This prospectively registered review searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through March 20, 2026, for diagnostic accuracy studies comparing two or more human-only or AI-integrated screening pathways using digital mammography or tomosynthesis. Bayesian bivariate random-effects network meta-analyses were fitted to a primary four-node and a secondary six-node network; risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 3 (QUADAS-3) and QUADAS-C tools, and certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Results Thirty-eight studies, with more than 4.2 million examinations, were included. In the primary digital mammography network (15 studies), AI as an independent reader (sensitivity, 78.9%; specificity, 95.8%) performed similarly to double human reading (sensitivity, 77.7%; specificity, 96.2%). In the secondary network, AI reader assistance had the highest sensitivity (86.8%) and AI triage had the highest specificity (96.4%). Per 10 000 screened (prevalence, 0.8%), AI reader assistance detected nine more cancers than single human reading (69 vs 60), with 77 additional false-positive recalls (558 vs 481); AI triage had 27% fewer false-positive recalls than single human reading (353 vs 481), with the same cancer detection as double human reading (64 vs 64). Stand-alone AI had the lowest specificity (93.0%) and the most false-positive recalls (n = 694). Rankings are hypothesis-generating: Top-ranked pathways had overlapping credible intervals. Conclusion In this synthesis, AI reader assistance was associated with the highest cancer detection and AI triage with the lowest false-positive recall; stand-alone AI was not supported as a primary screening strategy in settings with existing radiologist capacity. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Breast Cancer Screening, Diagnostic Test Accuracy, Deep Learning, Digital Mammography, Mammography, Network Meta-Analysis, Screening Pathway, Computer-aided Diagnosis Systematic review registration no. articles.title: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT in stage IV non-small cell lung cancer undergoing immune checkpoint blockade: Comparison to [18F]FDG PET/CT and role in response evaluation and prognosis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT and [18F]FDG PET/CT in patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and to explore the potential of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-derived parameters in evaluating treatment response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), as well as the association between total lesion (TL) FAPI and progression-free survival (PFS). METHODS: Twenty patients with stage IV NSCLC were prospectively included in this exploratory study. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT was performed at baseline and repeated after six weeks of ICB therapy. Baseline lesion uptake (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and target-to-background ratio (TBR)) were compared with previously performed [18F]FDG PET/CT. Baseline values and early changes in [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-derived parameters (ΔTLFAPI and primary tumour ΔSUVmax) were related to treatment response and evaluated in relation to PFS. RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT demonstrated a higher TBR than [18F]FDG PET/CT (all lesions analysed together: median TBR 7.34 vs. 5.05; p < 0.01), while SUVmax values did not differ significantly (median 9.42 vs. 9.13; p = 0.06). Early treatment responders showed marked reductions in TLFAPI whereas non-responders showed a median increase (median change - 50.41% vs. +10.11%; p = 0.01). Above-median baseline TLFAPI was associated with shorter PFS (HR 3.33, 95% CI 1.01-10.96; p = 0.048). CONCLUSION: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT confirmed its potential role in lesion detection. This exploratory study showed that early changes in TLFAPI might be associated with treatment response of ICB, and that baseline TLFAPI might be associated with PFS. Future studies on the role of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT in guiding ICB therapy would be of great interest.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Threshold optimization of artificial intelligence in digital breast tomosynthesis screening: a retrospective comparison study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of a deep learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) system for digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) screening and to compare its performance with radiologist-plus-CAD interpretation across multiple operating thresholds. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 1780 asymptomatic women who underwent screening DBT between July 2021 and June 2022. Radiologists interpreted examinations using BI-RADS, 5th edition; the AI system independently analyzed the examinations. Three operating thresholds were assessed: high-sensitivity threshold (HST) (≥ 2%), Youden index threshold (YIT) (≥ 27%), and recall rate-matched threshold (RMT) (≥ 36%). The reference standard was histopathologic confirmation for positive cases and a 24-month follow-up for negative cases. Sensitivity, specificity, and recall rates were compared using the McNemar test. RESULTS: Among 1780 women (mean age ± SD, 55.7 ± 7.4 years), 1469 (82.5%) had dense breasts (BI-RADS density category C or D). Eighteen cancers were confirmed: 12 screen-detected and 6 interval cancers (cancer rate in the cohort, 10.1 per 1000 examinations). At the YIT (≥ 27%), AI achieved numerically higher sensitivity than radiologist-plus-CAD (77.8% (14/18) vs 66.7% (12/18)), although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.457), with lower specificity (81.2% vs 95.2%; p < 0.001) and a higher recall rate (19.4% vs 5.4%; p < 0.001). Negative predictive value (NPV) was high for both (99.7% vs 99.6%). AI detected two of six interval cancers missed by radiologist-plus-CAD; four interval cancers were missed by both methods. CONCLUSION: Standalone AI performance was threshold-dependent, with numerically higher sensitivity but significantly lower specificity than radiologist-plus-CAD, requiring external validation given the limited sample. KEY POINTS: Question What is the optimal threshold for standalone artificial intelligence in digital breast tomosynthesis screening to balance cancer detection and recall rates? Findings Standalone artificial intelligence showed numerically higher sensitivity but significantly lower specificity than radiologist-plus-CAD (81.2% vs 95.2%), with threshold choice shaping detection and recall. Clinical relevance In digital breast tomosynthesis screening, standalone AI performance varied with the selected threshold. At the Youden threshold, AI maintained a high negative predictive value and detected 2 of 6 interval cancers; the small cancer sample limits conclusions about clinical benefit.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of MR arthrography for detecting adhesions after arthroscopic hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of MR arthrography for detecting postoperative intra-articular adhesions after hip arthroscopy (HAS) for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAIS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients undergoing hip MR arthrography from February 2015 through December 2025, followed by revision HAS within 180 days. Three radiologists independently assessed capsulofemoral and perilabral adhesions using predefined morphologic criteria. Two radiologists independently classified anterior and superolateral capsular distension as substantial or limited based on capsular convexity and contrast-filled separation from the femoral neck, respectively. Sensitivity, specificity, positive/negative predictive values, and accuracy with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using revision arthroscopy as the reference standard. Interreader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC2. RESULTS: Among 62 patients (mean age, 39 ± 9 years; 31 women), arthroscopy identified adhesions in 41 (66%), including capsulofemoral adhesions in 35 (56%) and perilabral adhesions in 17 (27%). Across readers, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 78-80%, 62-76%, and 73-77% for any adhesion; 71-77%, 63-81%, and 68-77% for capsulofemoral adhesions; and 65-76%, 80-87%, and 76-81% for perilabral adhesions, respectively. Interreader agreement was good and very good for capsulofemoral and perilabral adhesions (κ = 0.65 and 0.83, respectively). With substantial capsular distension, specificity and accuracy were numerically higher at 77-91% and 76-88% for capsulofemoral adhesions and 85-95% and 78-85% for perilabral adhesions, respectively. CONCLUSION: The diagnostic performance observed in our study supports the use of MR arthrography for the preoperative evaluation of suspected adhesions after HAS for FAIS, with good to very good interreader agreement for the assessment of capsulofemoral and perilabral adhesions. KEY POINTS: Question What is the diagnostic performance of MR arthrography for detecting postoperative adhesions in patients with persistent symptoms after arthroscopic surgery for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome? Findings Across three readers, MR arthrography demonstrated accuracies of 68-77% for capsulofemoral adhesions and 76-81% for perilabral adhesions, with good to very good interreader agreement. Clinical relevance MR arthrography supports preoperative evaluation of suspected adhesions in symptomatic patients after arthroscopic treatment of femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, providing clinically relevant diagnostic information for further management and revision arthroscopy planning.

articles.title: Phase-Resolved Functional Lung MRI: From Signal Formation to Clinical Interpretation.
articles.abstract: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides spatially resolved assessments of pulmonary ventilation and perfusion-related function from free-breathing proton MRI, without administering contrast agents or inhaled tracer gases. Interpreting these assessments requires a clear distinction between the measured signal and the physiological quantities inferred from it. This narrative review follows the measurement chain from pulmonary signal formation and sequence selection through acquisition, reconstruction, respiratory and cardiac phase assignment, image registration, biomarker derivation, and clinical interpretation. We examine ventilation-related signal changes, regional flow-volume loop metrics, perfusion weighting, model-dependent perfusion quantification, and threshold-defined defect percentages. Retrospectively reconstructed physiological cycles combine observations obtained during different breaths or heartbeats; their smooth appearance does not guarantee physiological fidelity. Moreover, regional signal modulation is not a direct measure of airflow, and cardiac weighting is not equivalent to absolute blood flow. Evidence from test-retest studies, multicenter comparisons, and comparisons with hyperpolarized xenon MRI, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, and nuclear medicine methods demonstrates useful regional information but also biomarker-specific limits of agreement and reproducibility. We review applications in obstructive, vascular, interstitial, transplant-related, and pediatric lung disease, illustrated by eight clinical cases. Volumetric and ultrashort echo-time acquisitions expand opportunities for regional ventilation mapping, although their validation does not automatically extend to cardiac-derived perfusion. Processing choices-including respiratory sorting, registration, segmentation, normalization, and defect thresholds-can alter reported values and their interpretation. PREFUL MRI thus provides a framework for deriving regional functional estimates, not an acquisition-independent physiological standard. Reliable translation requires harmonized protocols, transparent reporting of processing decisions, and validation of individual biomarkers against appropriate physiological and clinical endpoints.

articles.title: Disc-Reins-Wall classification of TFCC injuries: imaging correlates, pitfalls, and structured reporting using MRI and MR arthrography.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in arthroscopic anatomy have led to a three-dimensional understanding of the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC), organized around the articular disc, the distal radioulnar ligaments acting as stabilizing "reins," and the peripheral capsuloligamentous wall. Building on this updated anatomic concept, the Disc-Reins-Wall (D-R-W) classification provides a three-dimensional framework for mapping TFCC injuries according to the component involved and a description of combined injury patterns. TFCC injuries have historically been described using several classification systems, progressively expanded by the recognition of additional injury patterns, including deep foveal, radial, and peripheral lesions, further complicating their translation to imaging findings. Application of the D-R-W framework to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and MR arthrography relies on precise anatomic localization of the injured structure and multiplanar assessment adapted to the orientation of the different TFCC components. Disc injuries include degenerative and traumatic lesions; radioulnar ligament injuries include ulnar foveal and styloid abnormalities as well as different radial injury patterns; and wall injuries include peripheral capsuloligamentous and ulnocarpal lesions. Diagnostic challenges related to MRI include the difficulty in detection of longitudinal tears of the ulnotriquetral ligament, although MR arthrography may overcome some of these pitfalls. Recognition of anatomic variants, those changes related to a specific forearm position, and nonspecific imaging findings are essential to reduce false-positive findings, false-negative findings, and incorrect assignment of the precise site of injury. This review integrates the D-R-W classification system with imaging findings in order to facilitate meaningful communication between radiologists and hand surgeons.

articles.title: Automated Sacroiliac Joint Localization and Multilabel Classification of MRI Structural Lesions in Axial Spondyloarthritis: Multicenter External Validation and Radiologist Comparison.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Structural lesions of the sacroiliac joints (SIJs), including erosion, sclerosis, and ankylosis, are central imaging features in axial spondyloarthritis (AxSpA) but may be challenging to detect consistently on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), particularly for subtle or early abnormalities. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a deep learning pipeline that automatically localizes SIJs and classifies these three structural lesions, and to assess its performance against radiologists in a multicenter external validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective multicenter data from 833 patients with AxSpA were collected from three centers. Center A (n = 705) was divided into training (n = 587) and internal testing (n = 118) sets; Centers B and C formed the external test set (n = 128). Axial T1-weighted and oblique coronal fat-suppressed T1-weighted images were processed using an nnDetection-based three-dimensional detector and ResNet-50 classifier. Consensus radiologist assessment was the reference standard. Metrics included Dice coefficient, area under the free-response receiver operating characteristic curve (AUFROC), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity; gradient-weighted class activation mapping assessed interpretability. RESULTS: The detector achieved Dice coefficients >0.75 and AUFROC/AP@0.5 values >0.90. Internal-test AUCs were 0.866 for erosion, 0.848 for sclerosis, and 0.986 for ankylosis; external-test AUCs were 0.807, 0.822, and 0.970, respectively. In external testing, the model outperformed the junior radiologist for ankylosis detection: accuracy, 91.0% vs. 82.8%, p = 0.011; specificity, 91.2% vs. 80.3%, p < 0.01. Model performance was comparable with that of the senior radiologist. CONCLUSION: This automated, interpretable pipeline enabled multicenter MRI-based sacroiliac joint localization and structural lesion classification. External validation showed strongest stability for ankylosis, supporting its potential as a radiologist-assistive tool after prospective validation.

articles.title: The emotional impact of post-mortem imaging for the radiographer.
articles.abstract: Post-mortem (PM) imaging is increasingly used in investigations of suspicious and non-suspicious deaths, with radiographers responsible for image acquisition that may subsequently be relied upon in medico-legal investigations and court proceedings. While the technical and diagnostic aspects of PM imaging have been well described elsewhere, the psychosocial impact of this work on the radiographers undertaking image acquisition remains under-reported. Emotional responses to PM imaging arise not only from exposure to the deceased, but also from the accountability and responsibility associated with forensic imaging practice. Radiographers undertaking PM imaging describe a range of negative emotional responses associated with repeated exposure to traumatic injury, close physical interaction with the deceased, and the responsibility for producing images suitable for medico-legal investigations. Positive emotional responses from completing PM imaging have also been reported but are less widely recognised than the negative impact. Recognition of negative and positive responses, and the factors that contribute to them, alongside appropriate training and organisational support, is necessary to support radiographer well-being, and ensure sustained delivery of high-quality imaging in death investigations.

articles.title: Bone tumours with wash-out on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI: beyond giant cell tumour of bone.
articles.abstract: Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI is a well-known technique to characterise perfusion in bone tumours, yet the diagnostic value of the wash-out phenomenon-rapid peak enhancement followed by a decline in signal intensity-remains underappreciated in musculoskeletal imaging. Wash-out is characteristic of giant cell tumours of bone, and this enhancement pattern may aid both diagnosis and treatment response assessment. This critical review summarises current applications of DCE-MRI in bone tumours, explains its principles, and highlights key findings from recent literature. We based our results on a systematic literature search in PubMed performed in March 2025, using these keywords: (1) magnetic resonance imaging, (2) bone tumour, (3) perfusion/wash-out, and added relevant MeSH terms and synonyms. We identified nineteen different bone tumour entities for which time-intensity curves were shown. Tumours with wash-out were either benign or malignant, including osteosarcoma, multiple myeloma, bone metastases of several primary tumours, and rare neoplasms such as epithelioid haemangioma or Erdheim-Chester disease. Notably, wash-out does not reliably distinguish benign from malignant lesions due to overlapping perfusion characteristics. We highlighted the clinical utility of DCE-MRI in narrowing differential diagnoses, monitoring treatment response, and detecting recurrence, particularly in complex postoperative scenarios. We observed significant heterogeneity in time-intensity curve classification and interpretation between different studies. In summary, wash-out is an advanced MRI feature that occurs across a diverse spectrum of primary and metastatic bone tumours. Greater awareness of wash-out patterns beyond giant cell tumour of bone may serve to enhance diagnostic confidence, especially in challenging cases. KEY POINTS: Question We critically reviewed the literature on wash-out (dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) variable) in bone tumours to give an overview of entities demonstrating this perfusion characteristic. Findings Wash-out is not exclusive to giant cell tumour of bone and occurs in both benign and malignant primary bone tumours and in metastases. Critical relevance statement Wash-out on DCE-MRI is a valuable diagnostic feature present in a diverse spectrum of primary bone tumours and bone metastases. Greater awareness of wash-out patterns can enhance diagnostic confidence and help assess treatment response or tumour recurrence in challenging cases.

articles.title: Quantification of T1 and T2 Metabolite Relaxation Times in Healthy Brain at 7 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Quantify T1 and T2 relaxation times of brain metabolites from MR spectra acquired at 7 T in healthy volunteers in a single scan session. METHODS: MR spectroscopy (MRS) data were acquired using a 7 T Siemens Terra MR scanner with an 8-channel transmit, 32-channel receive array head coil (Nova Medical). Single-voxel MRS was acquired in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) and left frontal white matter (LFWM) using a semi-localized by adiabatic selective refocusing (sLASER) sequence with six inversion times (TIs) for T1 quantification (TI = 0, 1200, 1900, 2600, 3400, 4200 ms) and 7 echo times (TE) for T2 quantification (TE = 35, 70, 105, 140, 170, 270, 380 ms). Metabolite quantification was performed in LCModel (v6.3-1R). T1 and T2 relaxation times were calculated from a nonlinear least squares curve fit of metabolite concentration as a function of TI or TE, respectively. RESULTS: The final cohort included 21 healthy adults (35.2 ± 10.9 years old, 9 males/12 females). T1 and T2 times were quantified for 16 and 15 metabolite resonances, respectively, in both the PCC (n = 14) and LFWM (n = 7), including both -CH2 and -CH3 moieties of both total creatine + phosphocreatine and N-acetylaspartate. CONCLUSION: T1 and T2 relaxation times of multiple brain metabolites are reported and may be useful for optimizing MRS acquisition parameters and quantifying metabolite concentrations from spectra acquired at 7 T.

articles.title: Digital subtraction cardiac angiography by synthetic-mask energy subtraction: phantom demonstration for iodine and stent imaging.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) has limited application for cardiac angiography due to significant soft-tissue motion. Synthetic-mask approaches have been proposed previously, but they also suffer from soft-tissue motion artifacts. PURPOSE: Develop a synthetic-mask subtraction angiography technique for cardiac applications by suppressing soft-tissue structures using dual energy subtraction angiography (ESA) methods to prevent soft-tissue motion artifacts, and demonstrate in a phantom study for highlighting both contrasted arteries and stents. METHODS: Optimal parameters for kV-switching dual-energy ESA were determined theoretically including a calculation of expected signal and noise in the synthetic-mask angiograms. Results using a beam filter optimized for each kV separately were compared with those for a single stationary filter for both exposures. Synthetic-mask angiography was demonstrated on an anthropomorphic chest phantom with custom-designed coronary phantom overlays using high/low energy images acquired individually. RESULTS: Use of a stationary beam filter for both high and low-energy exposures, rather than two optimized filters, resulted in a 5-30% drop in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). This drop increased at very low exposure levels where detector readout noise becomes significant in the low-kV image. A maximum-value search through a sequence of post-injection ESA images showed greatly reduced soft-tissue motion artifacts compared to use of signal-energy images. The search added a bias to average pixel value and associated noise of less than 3%. CONCLUSIONS: Using thesynthetic-mask approach combined with dual-energy methods effectively eliminated soft-tissue motion artifacts and provided greatly enhanced images of contrasted arteries and stents in a phantom study. While the method requires motion of arteries and stent in the synthetic-mask calculation, six frames with motion modeled after a clinical sequence produced good results.

articles.title: A double-strand breaks complexity weighted approach for estimating the relative biological effectiveness of carbon ion beams.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The high relative biological effectiveness (RBE) of carbon-ion therapy is primarily attributed to the complexity of induced DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs). PURPOSE: We aim to establish a DSB complexity-weighted RBE model and quantify the contribution of different DSB types in carbon-ion therapy. METHOD: The DSB yields for polyenergetic mixed particle (Case I) and monoenergetic single particle carbon beams (Case II) across LET = 20-400 keV/µm were calculated via Monte-Carlo simulations. DSBs were classified according to the number n of additional strand breaks within a 10 base pair (bp) DNA segment adjacent to a single DSB, defined as DSB n = 0   , DSB n = 1   , and DSB n = 2 x   ( DSB n ≥ 2   ). Three weighting schemes were developed to calculate the complexity-weighted RBE ( RB E W   ). By considering different Cases or LET range, four fitting strategies were adopted to determine the weights of each DSB n  . RESULTS: Compared to the experimental data, the mean absolute error of RBE W  was decreased by up to 51.6% to that of equal weighted RBE. DSB n ≥ 1   exhibited twice the lethality of DSB n = 0   in the global fits. When considering the LET dependence of the weights, the lethality of DSB n ≥ 1   was approximately 3.5 times that of DSB n = 0   for LET < 150 keV/µm, and remained twice for LET > 150 keV/µm. CONCLUSION: The DSB complexity-weighted method showed good robustness across a wide LET range human salivary gland tumor (HSG) cells and high precision in describing the RBE of carbon ion beams. It was demonstrated that cell lethality was strongly correlated with the quantity and complexity of DSBs.

articles.title: Deuteron beam radiotherapy: A Monte Carlo study relative to protons and helium ions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Compared with heavier ions, protons undergo greater multiple scattering, resulting in a broader lateral penumbra that can increase dose to organs at risk (OARs) adjacent to the planning target volume (PTV). While heavier ions exhibit reduced lateral spread, their clinical use is limited by increased technical complexity and more demanding accelerator and beam transport requirements. Deuterons may provide an intermediate solution, offering reduced scattering compared with protons while potentially reducing these technical demands relative to heavier ions. PURPOSE: To assess the dosimetric potential and model-based relative biological effectiveness (RBE) of deuteron beams in comparison with protons and helium ions using Monte Carlo simulations. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations were performed using TOPAS with a simplified model of a clinical pencil beam scanning delivery system. Monoenergetic beams and spread-out Bragg peaks were generated for protons, deuterons, and helium ions. Depth-dose distributions, lateral beam spread, dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETD) and lineal energy (yD), and model-based RBE were evaluated. Dose-volume histograms (DVHs) for an idealized clinically relevant scenario were used to assess sparing of OARs adjacent to the PTV. Secondary neutron spectra and ambient dose equivalent (H*(10)) were also analyzed. RESULTS: Deuterons exhibited higher peak-to-plateau ratios than protons for Bragg peak depths below 6.1 cm and, than helium ions with ripple filter below 11.6 cm. Lateral beam spread was reduced compared with protons, with a 0.46 cm decrease in FWHM at 30.0 cm, while helium ions provided a further reduction of 0.26 cm. LETD increased from the entrance region to the distal fall-off, reaching up to 17.1, 19.6, and 33.6 keV µm- 1 for protons, deuterons, and helium ions, corresponding to RBE values up to 1.63, 1.70, and 2.53, respectively. DVH analysis showed lateral OAR mean doses of 50.5, 46.5, and 43.5 Gy for protons, deuterons, and helium ions, respectively. The ambient dose equivalent H*(10) was highest for deuterons, reaching up to 10.7 mSv Gy- 1, approximately 5.7 and 1.6 times higher than for protons and helium ions, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Deuterons exhibit properties intermediate between protons and helium ions, with lateral dose characteristics closer to helium and RBE closer to protons. These findings suggest that deuterons may offer a favorable balance between dose conformity, biological effectiveness, and technical complexity, warranting further investigation in clinically realistic settings.

articles.title: Scientific productivity of the Eastern European countries in imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Scientific productivity in Europe shows considerable variation, particularly between Eastern and Western countries. Radiology and imaging research has expanded rapidly in recent years, yet the distribution of scientific output across Europe remains unexplored. This study aimed to systematically assess the scientific performance of European countries in the field of radiology and imaging, with a specific focus on disparities between Eastern and Western Bloc countries and the underlying contributing factors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Scientometric data were retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases covering the period from 1996 to 2021. Metrics included publication counts, citations, H-index, and highly cited papers. Economic indicators, research and development (R&D) expenditure, education levels, and imaging infrastructure were analysed for correlation with scientific performance. RESULTS: Western European countries demonstrated higher scientific output and impact in radiology and imaging compared to Eastern countries (p < 0.001). Publications, citations, and H-index values were higher in the West. Associations were observed between scientific productivity and economic strength (GDP per capita) (p < 0.05), R&D intensity (p < 0.05), and the proportion of highly educated individuals employed in science and technology (p < 0.05). Temporal analysis also demonstrated that past scientific performance was associated with subsequent publication volume. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal persistent disparities in radiology research productivity between Eastern and Western Europe, which are associated with differences in economic capacity, educational factors and research infrastructure. Addressing these imbalances may benefit from coordinated investments, promotion of scientific networks, and targeted initiatives by national governments, the European Union, and professional societies such as the European Society of Radiology to strengthen research capacity and knowledge transfer across Europe. KEY POINTS: How does radiology and imaging research productivity vary across European countries, and how do economic, research, and educational characteristics relate to these differences? Western Europe shows higher publication output, citation impact, and H-index, while research productivity was correlated with economic, R&D, and educational indicators. Critical Relevance Statement This study describes geographic differences in European radiology research productivity and examines their relationships with economic, research, and educational characteristics. These findings provide a comparative perspective on research capacity across Europe and may inform efforts to strengthen collaboration and development.

articles.title: Novel toilet filtration system for contrast material removal at the source: first outpatient results.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Iodinated contrast media (ICM) are essential for diagnostic imaging but impose a substantial environmental burden due to their widespread use. This prospective observational study evaluates the efficiency of a novel toilet filtration system (TFS) for recovering ICM after contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) and explores factors that contribute to successful implementation of the system. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective observational study included consecutive outpatients scheduled for ceCT using Iomeprol as ICM. Patients were informed about the TFS, ICM excretion, and environmental implications. They were asked to wait at least 30 min after scanning and to use the TFS for their first post-ceCT urination. The removal efficiency of the TFS was determined by measuring ICM concentrations in influent and effluent streams. The proportion of administered ICM recovered was calculated from the cartridge's contents. RESULTS: Of 395 consecutive patients undergoing ceCT, 277 (70%) consented to participate, and 273 patients (median age 65.5; IQR: 57.2-73.4; 151 men) successfully used the TFS. The median interval between contrast administration and urination was 36 min (IQR: 31-41). Most patients (81%) waited at least 30 min before voiding. Removal efficiency of the TFS exceeded 99.9% for ICM. Limited ICM excretion led to recovery of 2.78 kg out of 18.41 kg administered Iomeprol (15.1%; 1.36 kg iodine). CONCLUSION: While ICM is efficiently removed using a novel TFS (> 99.9%), ICM excretion during the 30-min post-examination waiting period was limited. The approach can recover approximately 71 kg of ICM per year per 10,000 ceCT examinations, a number that could be further improved through efforts to increase ICM excretion. KEY POINTS: Question TFS have the potential to reduce the amount of contrast media entering wastewater, but their effectiveness is unclear. Findings TFS achieved excellent contrast removal, and was well accepted by patients, but contrast excretion within the median 36-min waiting period is limited to 15%. Critical relevance statement The novel toilet-based filtration system enables substantial iodine recovery from excreted ICM in urine, but limited post-ceCT excretion during short waiting times highlights the need for process adaptations to further increase overall excretion and maximise iodine recovery rates.

articles.title: CT-based Simple Scoring System for the Diagnosis and Risk Stratification of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma in Small Solid Renal Masses: Comparison With a Conventional CT Algorithm.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop a simple computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for diagnosing clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) in small (≤4 cm) solid renal masses, compare its performance with an existing CT algorithm, and perform patient risk stratification. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 372 pathologically confirmed small solid renal masses, which were randomly divided into derivation (n = 223) and validation (n = 149) cohorts. Two radiologists independently assessed CT features. Independent predictors were identified using multivariate regression to construct the scoring system. Receiver operating characteristic analysis compared diagnostic performance, and four risk strata were defined. Correlations between radiomic features were assessed using Spearman's correlation analysis. RESULTS: The scoring system included five predictors: sex, Major/Minor axis ratio, standardized heterogeneity ratio, mass-to-cortex corticomedullary attenuation ratio, and relative corticomedullary-to-nephrographic washout ratio. It outperformed the comparator CT-score in derivation (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]: 0.899 vs. 0.755, p < 0.001) and validation cohorts (AUC: 0.914 vs. 0.774, p < 0.001). At cut-off >6, our system versus comparator CT-score yielded: derivation cohort sensitivity 86.3% versus 67.8%, negative predictive value (NPV) 75.9% versus 57.7%; validation cohort sensitivity 88.8% versus 70.4%, NPV 79.2% versus 59.7%. Predicted risks were generally comparable to observed risks across the four risk strata. CT features correlated well with corresponding radiomic features (R range, -0.618-0.743; p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This simple CT feature-based scoring system achieves excellent ccRCC diagnostic performance, outperforms a conventional CT algorithm, and supports reliable noninvasive diagnosis and risk stratification.

articles.title: Nonoverlapping Peritumoral CT Radiomics and Overall Survival in TACE-treated Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An Exploratory Association Study with Selection-aware Internal Validation.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The hepatoma arterial-embolization prognostic (HAP) score and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage do not capture spatial heterogeneity at the tumor-liver interface in hepatocellular carcinoma treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). We assessed whether computed tomography (CT) radiomic features from three nonoverlapping peritumoral zones are associated with survival and whether discrimination gain over HAP and BCLC survives selection-aware validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Arterial-phase CT segmentations from the public Warsaw (WAW)-TACE dataset were analyzed retrospectively in 110 patients (75 deaths). Tumor and peritumoral-shell features (0-3, 3-5, 5-10 mm) were screened with false-discovery-rate-corrected Cox regression; three gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) ratio features entered a Cox model with HAP and BCLC (fixed three-feature model). Selection-aware validation used repeated cross-validation, 100 70/30 splits, and penalized Cox models. RESULTS: Three GLCM ratio features passed FDR screening (univariate q = 0.006-0.029) and remained associated with survival (hazard ratios 1.32-1.68; p values conditional on selection), after adjustment for tumor size, surface area, and multifocality (p < 0.01). Apparent 3-year area under the curve was 0.753 versus 0.691 for HAP + BCLC. When selection was repeated on training data, no advantage remained (C-index 0.645 vs. 0.670; better than HAP + BCLC in 19% of splits); penalized models retained no stable feature. CONCLUSION: Peritumoral texture ratios showed associations with survival after TACE, independent of tumor size, supporting further study of the tumor-liver interface. Incremental predictive value beyond HAP and BCLC was not demonstrated after selection-aware validation. These hypothesis-generating findings require independent confirmation in external data.

articles.title: Tumefactive demyelinating lesions in patients with systemic malignancy: case series and review of the literature.
articles.abstract: Imaging characteristics, clinical manifestations, and prognosis of tumefactive demyelinating lesions (TDL) have been extensively described. The coexistence of TDL with systemic malignancy as a paraneoplastic phenomenon is uncommon and important for the neuroradiologist to recognize. We present a retrospective, single-center case series of 7 patients (5 pathology-proven cases) who presented with TDL and concomitant systemic malignancy and describe their imaging findings, associated primary neoplasms, instaurated treatments and chronologic timeline with respect to cancer diagnosis. Our findings indicate that hematologic and germ cell neoplasms are malignancies which may manifest with concomitant TDL.

articles.title: Remote Flow Diversion for Intracranial Aneurysms: Safety and Efficacy Outcomes from a Single-center Cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Remote flow diversion (RFD), defined as flow-diverter (FD) deployment without direct coverage of the aneurysm neck, has emerged as a therapeutic alternative for aneurysms arising from eccentric bifurcations or distal branches. We aimed to evaluate angiographic and safety outcomes of RFD and compare them with those of conventional FD techniques (complete or partial neck coverage). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained single-center registry of all intracranial aneurysms treated with FDs between January 2018 and March 2025. Neck coverage was classified as complete, partial, or absent (RFD) per international consensus criteria. Primary outcomes included complete occlusion (Raymond-Roy class I) at last angiographic follow-up, permanent morbidity, and mortality. Covered-branch patency was also assessed. RESULTS: RFD was used in 20/305 (6.6%) aneurysms, predominantly located at the MCA (45.0%), followed by the ACA/ACoA (30.0%), carotid artery (15.0%), and posterior circulation (10.0%). Complete occlusion was achieved in 16/20 (80.0%; 95% CI, 56.3-94.3%). Among the 12 aneurysms treated with RFD without previous or concomitant aneurysm-directed treatment, complete occlusion was achieved in 12/12 (100%; 95% CI, 73.5-100%). Intraprocedural complications occurred in 3/20 cases (15.0%; 95% CI, 3.2-37.9%). Branch occlusion occurred in 3/20 cases (15.0%; 95% CI, 3.2-37.9%) and branch stenosis in 11/20 (55.0%; 95% CI, 31.5-76.9%). One patient experienced transient neurological symptoms and another a delayed increase in mRS of 1 point; however, no permanent procedure-related morbidity (mRS increase > 1 point; 0%; 95% CI, 0-16.8%) or procedure-related mortality (0%; 95% CI, 0-16.8%) was observed. Occlusion rates were 46.1% in the partial coverage group (76 aneurysms) and 76.1% in the complete coverage group (209 aneurysms) (p < 0.001), whereas morbidity rates were 2.6% and 3.3%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, RFD was associated with complete aneurysm occlusion in most cases, without observed permanent procedure-related morbidity or mortality. These findings support its consideration in selected aneurysms for which direct neck coverage is technically challenging or anatomically unfavorable, but require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Pallister-Hall Syndrome among Pediatric Patients with Hypothalamic Hamartoma: Neuroimaging Features and Cochlear Manifestations.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Pallister-Hall syndrome (PHS) is a rare developmental disorder characterized by hypothalamic hamartoma and digital abnormalities. The hamartoma may provide the first clue to the underlying syndrome. We aimed to characterize the clinical and neuroimaging features of pediatric PHS, with attention to cochlear abnormalities. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study reviewed 164 pediatric patients with hypothalamic hamartoma. Patients meeting clinical or genetic criteria for PHS were included. Clinical and genetic data were collected, and 2 independent pediatric radiologists evaluated available MR imaging for hamartoma morphology, signal characteristics, enhancement, diffusion, associated abnormalities, and cochlear morphology. RESULTS: Eight patients met the study criteria for PHS (4.9%). Median age was 2 years (range, 1-14 years). A pathogenic GLI3 variant was documented in 4 patients. PHS was diagnosed only after hamartoma detection in all patients. All had digital abnormalities and seizures or epilepsy; 6 had endocrine abnormalities, most commonly precocious puberty. Cochlear abnormalities occurred in 2 patients and sensorineural hearing loss in 1 and bifid epiglottis in 1. All hamartomas were centered at the tuber cinereum or floor of the third ventricle, were isointense to gray matter on T1- and T2-weighted imaging and demonstrated no enhancement or restricted diffusion. CONCLUSIONS: Recognition of PHS-associated hypothalamic hamartomas may prompt syndromic diagnosis and targeted clinical evaluation. Cochlear abnormalities may represent an underrecognized component of PHS requiring confirmation in larger molecularly characterized cohorts.

articles.title: Medium Vessel Occlusion In the Era of Conflicting Trials: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for MeVO have been published, yielding conflicting results. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize available randomized evidence comparing EVT plus best medical treatment (BMT) versus BMT alone in patients with acute MeVO. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central for RCTs comparing EVT with BMT in patients with MeVO. The primary outcome was functional independence (mRS 0-2 at 90 days). Secondary outcomes included excellent functional recovery (mRS 0-1), all-cause mortality, and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), and any intracranial hemorrhage. Pooled risk ratios (RR) were calculated using random-effects models. RESULTS: Four RCTs were included, enrolling 1,879 patients (929 EVT + BMT, 950 BMT). There was no difference in functional independence at 90 days (mRS 0-2: RR 1.02, 95%CI 0.81-1.30) or excellent functional recovery (mRS 0-1: RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.77-1.59). No significant difference in all-cause mortality was observed (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.76-1.77). EVT was associated with an increased risk of sICH compared with BMT alone, although with wide uncertainty (RR 2.54, 95% CI 1.17-5.53). EVT was also associated with more subarachnoid hemorrhage (RR 6.20, 95% CI 1.76-21.82) and any intracranial hemorrhage (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.17-2.51). Exploratory trial-level meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between baseline NIHSS and treatment effect. CONCLUSION: EVT did not improve functional outcomes compared with BMT alone in patients with MeVO stroke, while being associated with an increased risk of sICH. The ORIENTAL-MeVO results suggest that baseline stroke severity may be a critical effect modifier, with higher NIHSS scores conferring greater benefit from EVT. Treatment decisions for MeVO patients should be individualized, balancing the trade-off of potential risks and benefits.

articles.title: Bayesian CT Perfusion Restores the Clinical Utility of Mean Transit Time in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Mean transit time (MTT) is a comprehensive perfusion parameter that reflects blood transit through the arterial, capillary, and venous compartments of the cerebral circulation. Despite its physiologic advantages, MTT has been largely replaced by perfusion parameters such as time-to-maximum (Tmax) due to its noisy nature and poorly interpretable maps. We hypothesized that Bayesian postprocessing, which is inherently less sensitive to image noise, could restore the clinical utility of MTT by improving image quality and providing reliable quantitative estimates of hypoperfused tissue. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large or medium vessel occlusion who underwent CT perfusion (CTP). CTP datasets were processed using two commercially available SVD-based implementations and a Bayesian method. Two board-certified neuroradiologists, blinded to postprocessing method, assessed image quality using a 4-point scale based on noise, distortion, and delineation of hypoperfusion, with scores ≥3 considered diagnostic. Reader confidence and identification of the affected hemisphere were also assessed. Quantitative analysis compared hypoperfused tissue volumes derived from relative MTT (rMTT ≥1.4) using Bayesian and SVD processing with Tmax >6 seconds. Agreement was evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were included. Bayesian-generated MTT maps demonstrated significantly higher image quality than either SVD implementation (both P<.01) and were considered diagnostic in 71.2% of evaluations. The affected side was not correctly identified in 5.8% (9/156) of Bayesian-MTT evaluations, compared with 50.4% (64/127) for SVD-1 and 71.8% (112/156) for SVD-2 (P<.01). Median hypoperfused tissue volume using Tmax >6 seconds was 103 mL (IQR, 67-131 mL), compared with 91 mL (IQR, 62-127 mL) for Bayesian-MTT and 25 mL (IQR, 14-37 mL) for SVD-MTT. The mean (SD) volume difference between Bayesian-MTT and Tmax was 2.9 ± 35.0 mL (P=.20), whereas SVD-MTT underestimated hypoperfused tissue by 74.0 ± 46.0 mL (P<.01) relative to Tmax. CONCLUSIONS: Bayesian postprocessing substantially improves diagnostic image quality compared with conventional SVD-based methods and provides hypoperfusion volume estimates with closer agreement to the clinically established Tmax >6-second comparator. The marked differences between Bayesian- and SVD-derived MTT estimates highlight the substantial influence of the underlying deconvolution method on quantitative MTT assessment.

articles.title: Hierarchical structure-function decoupling in primary open-angle glaucoma reveals sensorimotor and frontoparietal network coupling abnormalities: A multimodal imaging and transcriptomic study.
articles.abstract: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is increasingly recognized as a neurodegenerative disease involving widespread brain alterations beyond the visual system. We used the structural decoupling index (SDI) to characterize structure-function coupling abnormalities in POAG and investigated their spatial associations with neurotransmitter systems and transcriptomic profiles. We recruited 70 POAG patients and 44 matched healthy controls. All underwent diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI). SDI quantifies the dependence of regional activity on white matter structure. After identifying group differences in SDI, we examined their spatial associations with normative neurotransmitter distributions and cortical gene expression profiles using partial least squares (PLS) regression. Compared with controls, POAG patients exhibited significantly increased SDI in 30 regions spanning unimodal, transmodal and subcortical areas. These alterations were predominantly distributed within the sensorimotor network (SMN) and frontoparietal network (FPN). The most significant associations were observed for NAT and 5-HT1a. SDI alterations were associated with cortical gene expression patterns and showed overlap with previously reported POAG-associated genes. Enrichment analyses revealed distinct molecular signatures, with PLS1+ genes enriched in mitochondrial-related processes and MAPK signaling, whereas PLS1- genes were associated with neuronal and synaptic processes. This study provides evidence for hierarchical alterations in structure-function coupling in POAG and their molecular associations. The SDI elevations in SMN and FPN may reflect broader alterations in large-scale brain organization associated with POAG. These findings suggest that SDI may be sensitive to POAG-related brain alterations and may provide a framework for investigating the neural mechanisms underlying POAG.

articles.title: Image-guided setup, residual positional deviations, and intrafraction motion in pediatric extracranial proton therapy: A prospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite broad adoption of volumetric image guidance, quantitative and anatomicsite-specific measurementsof residual positional deviations and intrafraction motion in pediatric extracranial proton therapy remain limited. This prospective study quantified these parameters to inform data-drivenscenario-based optimizationand immobilization practices. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Between 2020 and 2024, 124 pediatric patients (median age at treatment, 11 years; 50% treated under anesthesia) receiving extracranial proton therapy were enrolled ina prospective institutional imaging protocol. Daily cone-beam CT (CBCT) was acquired for image-guided setup corrections, followed by a post-correction CBCT performed once per courseprior to treatment to quantify residual positional deviations. Weekly post-treatment CBCT assessed intrafraction motion.Paired 2D orthogonal radiographs and CBCT scans were obtained in 34 imaging cases, predominantly for thorax/abdomen and pelvis treatments. RESULTS: Daily CBCT-guided correction reduced median positional deviations from6.5 mmbefore correction to a residual0.9 mmacross treatment sites.At thepatientlevel,the95th percentile deviationsacross all sites were 2.7 mm (anesthetized), 5.3 mm (awake), and 4.2 mm (overall). At the scan level, the 95th percentile end-of-fraction deviation exceeded5 mmin awake patients treated at thorax/abdomen and pelvis sites whileremainingbelow3 mmunder anesthesia. In the paired-imaging subgroup, the median 3D vector difference between radiograph- and CBCT-derived corrections was 2.5 mm. CONCLUSIONS: CBCT-based image guidance improves setupaccuracy in extracranial proton therapy.The observed end-of-fraction positional deviations provide empirical measures of geometric uncertainty that may inform setup perturbations for scenario-based optimization and robustness assessment.

articles.title: Limited incremental value of radiomics in differentiating benign and malignant solid pulmonary nodules: Dominance of clinicoradiological features in a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the relative predictive contribution and incremental value of radiomic features and clinicoradiological features for discriminating benign from malignant solid pulmonary nodules within a multicenter machine learning framework. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 3,263 patients with pathologically confirmed solid pulmonary nodules were included. Patients from four centers in Zhejiang Province were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 1,958) and an internal validation cohort (n = 490), while an independent cohort from Anhui Province served as the external test cohort (n = 815). Radiomics features were extracted from CT images to feature selection, and the final 12 radiomic features were directly used as independent input variables to construct radiomics models using five machine learning algorithms: logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and categorical boosting (CatBoost). Independent clinicoradiological predictors were identified using logistic regression, and clinicoradiological models were subsequently constructed using the same five machine learning algorithms. After determining the optimal model for each feature domain, the optimal fusion weight was identified to construct a weighted fusion model. The diagnostic performance of the models was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: The clinicoradiological CatBoost model achieved AUCs of 0.912, 0.902, and 0.897 in the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. Among the radiomics models, XGBoost demonstrated the best overall performance, with AUCs of 0.767, 0.732, and 0.769 across the three cohorts, respectively. The weighted fusion model combining the clinicoradiological CatBoost and radiomics XGBoost models achieved AUCs of 0.883, 0.898, and 0.903 in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, respectively.
