In the external test cohort, the AUC of the fusion model increased from 0.897 to 0.903 compared with the clinicoradiological model; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.061). CONCLUSIONS: In the discrimination of benign and malignant solid pulmonary nodules, clinicoradiological features demonstrated greater discriminative performance than radiomic features. Even when the 12 radiomic features were directly incorporated into machine learning models, radiomics provided limited incremental value beyond clinicoradiological information. Radiomics may serve as a complementary source of quantitative information to clinicoradiological models, although its additional clinical benefit warrants further validation.

articles.title: Automated Hoffa-region MRI radiomics discriminates MOAKS-graded inflammation at Osteoarthritis Initiative scale.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: External generalisability limits MRI radiomics for knee osteoarthritis. We evaluated whether automated Hoffa-region MRI radiomics reproduces MOAKS at Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) scale, transfers externally, and signals 24-month joint-space progression. METHODS: We analysed 2,232 OAI baseline knees on sagittal 3D dual-echo steady-state (DESS) MRI and 2,098 paired intermediate-weighted turbo spin-echo acquisitions. 107 PyRadiomics features were computed on an automated Hoffa-region ROI. Discrimination used nested 5 × 5 L2-penalised logistic regression with ComBat-style harmonisation and locked-coefficient external transfer (n = 232). Prognosis used a 291-knee FNIH bridge and the 3,084-knee OAI cohort with Fine-Gray models treating total knee replacement and death as competing events. RESULTS: Hoffa-region radiomics added ΔAUC + 0.053 (95% CI + 0.037 to + 0.070) over a clinical baseline AUC of 0.734 for composite MOAKS inflammation ≥ 1, and + 0.032 (+0.021 to + 0.043) over a clinical + MOAKS-structural baseline. In the 232-knee external cohort the locked model added + 0.122 (+0.085 to + 0.157) cross-sectionally and + 0.076 (+0.041 to + 0.111, FWER-adjusted p < 0.001) for 24-month joint-space progression. Internal prognostic analyses diverged: incremental discrimination in the 291-knee FNIH bridge did not survive multiplicity (adjusted p = 0.142), whereas association with time-to-progression in the full 3,084-knee cohort was significant (Fine-Gray subdistribution HR 1.60, 1.23 to 2.08, p < 0.001, top-versus-bottom quintile; cumulative-incidence difference 12.4 percentage points, 6.3 to 18.0, at 96 months). The adjusted per-SD subdistribution hazard ratio was not significant (1.09, 0.99 to 1.20, p = 0.069). CONCLUSIONS: Automated Hoffa-region MRI radiomics provides reproducible MOAKS-aligned discrimination at OAI scale and replicates externally. The locked model is scoped to non-fat-saturated sequences. The joint-space-progression signal is a significant association under competing risks but its incremental value remains internally provisional, requiring prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Gaussian representation-based dynamic reconstruction and motion estimation framework for time-resolved volumetric MR imaging (DREME-GSMR).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Time-resolved volumetric MR imaging that reconstructs a 3D MRI within sub-seconds to resolve deformable motion is essential for motion-adaptive radiotherapy. Representing patient anatomy and associated motion fields as 3D Gaussians, we developed a spatiotemporal Gaussian representation-based framework (DREME-GSMR), which enables time-resolved dynamic MRI reconstruction from a pre-treatment 3D MR scan without any prior anatomical/motion model. APPROACH: DREME-GSMR represents a reference MRI volume and a corresponding low-rank motion model (as motion-basis components) using 3D Gaussians, and incorporates a dual-path MLP/CNN motion encoder to estimate temporal motion coefficients of the motion model from raw k-space-derived signals. Using the solved motion model, DREME-GSMR can infer motion coefficients directly from new online k-space data, enabling subsequent intra-treatment volumetric MR imaging and motion tracking (real-time imaging). A motion-augmentation strategy is further introduced to improve robustness to unseen motion patterns during real-time imaging. MAIN RESULTS: DREME-GSMR was evaluated on the XCAT digital phantom, a physical motion phantom, and MR-LINAC datasets acquired from 6 healthy volunteers and 20 patients (with independent sequential scans for cross-evaluation). DREME-GSMR produced time-resolved MRIs at a ~400 ms temporal resolution, with an inference time of ~10 ms/volume. In XCAT experiments, DREME-GSMR achieved mean(s.d.) SSIM, tumor center-of-mass error (COME), and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.92(0.01)/0.91(0.02), 0.50(0.15)/0.65(0.19) mm, and 0.92(0.02)/0.92(0.03) for dynamic reconstruction/real-time imaging. For the physical phantom, the mean target COME was 1.20(0.94)/1.40(1.15) mm for dynamic/real-time imaging, while for volunteers and patients, where no ground truth is available, the mean real-time liver COME relative to a dynamic reconstruction-derived pseudo-ground truth was 1.31(0.82) and 0.96(0.64) mm, respectively. SIGNIFICANCE: Evaluated on digital simulations and MR-LINAC measurements, DREME-GSMR enables sub-second 3D dynamic MRI reconstruction and real-time volumetric motion tracking from stack-of-stars k-space data, supporting intra-treatment motion-adaptive MR-guided radiotherapy.

articles.title: A scalable data acquisition architecture for multi-gantry long-axial-field-of-view PET systems.
articles.abstract: To develop and evaluate a scalable data acquisition chain (SDAC) for multi-gantry long-axial-field-of-view (LAFOV) PET systems, decoupling lines-of-response (LOR) growth from processing complexity and supporting multiple axial configurations without hardware reconfiguration.Approach: The SDAC consolidates axial detector data in data combined units (DCUs) prior to centralized coincidence processing; each DCU applies round-robin arbitration to single events from axially adjacent detector modules and tags every output packet with module and gantry identifiers. The architecture was implemented on a multi-gantry PET platform and evaluated in 2-, 3-, and 4-gantry configurations through count-rate measurements, analytical loss modeling, and an anthropomorphic phantom simulation.Main results: FPGA LUT and Register utilization was reduced by 52% and 63%, respectively, relative to a cross-coincidence implementation. Data loss at peak noise-equivalent count rate ranged from 1.25% (2-gantry) to 3.00% (4-gantry), with linear activity dependence. The analytical data-loss model agreed with measured module counts to within ~0.1%, with no significant activity dependence. In a single-realization XCAT phantom simulation (185 MBq 18F-FDG, four VOIs), count retention ranged from 99.0%-99.2% (Model B) and 96.2%-96.7% (Model C) relative to the no-dead-time baseline. The cross-VOI retention spread was within inter-VOI count-level variability, indicating no position-dependent bias exceeding intrinsic count-level dependence in this simulation; repeated simulations and clinical data are required to establish uniformity under broader activity distributions.Significance: The SDAC enables incremental axial coverage expansion while keeping the coincidence processor unchanged, lowering a practical barrier to LAFOV PET adoption. The analytical data-loss model supports a configuration-independent dead-time correction applicable to the 2-4 gantry configurations validated here, facilitating more practical system-level correction, and is plausibly extensible to higher gantry counts.

articles.title: Preoperative CT-based topological intratumoral heterogeneity for predicting microvascular invasion and recurrence risk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: We developed and validated a portal venous phase CT-based model that combines topological intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH), radiomics, and clinicoradiological features for preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We also examined whether three-dimensional (3D) ITH was associated with transcriptomic and immune-related features in an exploratory radiogenomic cohort. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 821 surgically confirmed HCC patients in training (n = 489), internal validation (n = 211), and external validation (n = 121) cohorts. Manually segmented tumors were used to develop clinical, ITH, radiomics, and stacking ensemble models. Time to recurrence (TTR) and SHAP-based model interpretation were analyzed; mortality data were not collected, and death was therefore not incorporated into this recurrence endpoint. A separate supplementary, hypothesis-generating analysis of 42 TCGA-LIHC cases explored transcriptomic correlates of 3D ITH; differential-expression and gene-set analyses used Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate (FDR) correction. RESULTS: The ensemble achieved AUCs of 0.805 (95% CI, 0.760-0.847), 0.851 (95% CI, 0.796-0.902), and 0.757 (95% CI, 0.648-0.855) in the training out-of-fold, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The ITH model showed comparable and numerically slightly higher AUCs than the radiomics model, but paired DeLong tests did not show statistically significant differences. SHAP analysis ranked the 3D ITH score as the leading contributor within the ensemble, and both the 3D ITH score and ensemble risk score were associated with TTR. The supplementary TCGA-LIHC analysis generated exploratory associations between 3D ITH and survival and pathway-level transcriptomic patterns. CONCLUSIONS: Portal venous CT-derived topological ITH provided interpretable information for preoperative MVI prediction and recurrence-risk assessment in HCC. The supplementary radiogenomic observations are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Contrast-Enhancing Tumor Margin Detection in Gliomas using Non-Contrast MRI: From Human-Only to Human-AI Assisted Assessment.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Contrast-enhanced MRI is the cornerstone of neuro-oncological imaging, but concerns regarding sustainability and cost prompted interest in the development of gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA)-free alternatives. We investigated the ability of human raters to guess the tumor core in glioblastoma using GBCA-free MRI and evaluated the performance of AI-assisted segmentation. METHODS: A segmentation model was trained using BraTS (n = 989) and UCSF-PDGM (n = 501) datasets. Reference standard segmentations of the tumor core were generated using an established algorithm and corrected by an independent neuroradiologist. T1-weighted (T1w), T2-weighted (T2w), T2-FLAIR, DWI-B0 and B-1000, ADC MRI of 117 glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, patients were independently re-segmented by three radiologists and one non-clinician. Another radiologist (R-AI) improved segmentations produced by an AI algorithm without post-contrast sequence input. Statistical analysis compared AI segmentations with human performance. RESULTS: All raters showed a moderate-to-strong correlation with the reference standard (r = 0.79; P < 0.001). The AI-assisted reader achieved a higher Dice similarity by 0.09 (0.82 vs. 0.72; P < 0.001), greatly reduced Hausdorff distance (9.97 vs. 16.16 mm; P < 0.001), and decreased absolute volume error by 10.3 ml (6.75 vs. 17.07 ml; P < 0.001). Rater confidence increased with larger tumor volume, despite nonsignificant volumetric error metrics after correction (all P ≥ 0.24). Dice similarity did not differ significantly between the AI-assisted reader and the standalone AI model. CONCLUSION: Human raters delineated the tumor core from GBCA-free sequences with moderate accuracy, showing considerable inter-rater variability in glioblastoma. AI-assisted segmentation demonstrated promising tumor core identification, suggesting potential clinical utility, although its effect on human segmentation accuracy requires further investigation.

articles.title: FDG PET/CT After One Cycle of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Predicts Residual Cancer Burden in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
The PRIMARY2 Trial: PSMA PET/CT to Reduce Prostate Biopsy after Equivocal or Nonsuspicious MRI.
Effects of MR Sampling on Object Detection.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To provide a framework relating resolution and k-space sampling to human detection of objects and a new signal-to-noise metric more directly related to detection. THEORY AND METHODS: An analytic form to predict detectability of an object dependent on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), resolution, and sampling trajectory was proposed. A perception task and detection task were generated using images with synthetic noise. RESULTS: Subjects selected images to be perceptually more similar if they had the same SNR using the new metric rather than the conventional metric. Subjects had greater accuracy of detecting circles when looking at images simulating noise from non-Cartesian images. A detectability threshold using the new SNR metric was optimized to determine the minimum SNR and object size necessary to be detected. CONCLUSION: The new SNR metric may be more directly related to perception and detection. The framework may be useful in predicting object detection from arbitrary sampling trajectories.

articles.title: Tradeoff tuning via continuous organ-at-risk priority input for AI-Generated intensity-modulated radiation therapy plans for head-and-neck cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In current clinical practice, tradeoffs in treatment planning are handled by using multi-criteria optimization (MCO) algorithms or manual operations; very few AI models are capable of handling tradeoffs. PURPOSE: To design an Artificial Intelligence (AI) system that generates fluence maps with tunable tradeoffs, and to examine its performance in head-and-neck (HN) intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) treatment. METHODS: User-tunable, continuous organ-at-risk (OAR) priorities were conditioned into an AI-driven auto-planning system that predicts fluence maps for IMRT plans. Two separate AI models were developed and assembled sequentially for the auto-planning process. The first model predicted individual IMRT field dose using anatomy, tradeoff preferences, and beam configurations as inputs, followed by the second model that generated fluence maps. The two models were trained independently before being integrated for automatic plan generation. A total of 230 patients were included in this study (200/5/25 for training/validation/testing). Two IMRT plans were generated for each training case. One used a set of original priorities adopted from clinical planning template that had balanced dose tradeoffs among OARs and planning target volume (PTV); the other used the same set of dose-volume objectives while OAR sparing priorities were randomly altered by up to ± 20%. To examine the AI system's performance, three tests were designed to examine AI plans with a wide range of OAR priorities under different clinical scenarios. RESULTS: All AI plans using original OAR priorities have clinically acceptable dose distributions. As the OAR priorities change, dose distributions and dose volume histograms (DVHs) in the AI plans change accordingly within the -40% to +80% adjustment range. The dose metrics in AI plans have monotonic response to the corresponding input priorities, with high priorities achieving more sparing. Subtle secondary dose tradeoffs among OARs are also observed. CONCLUSIONS: The AI system can generate substantially different AI plans for the same patient according to the OAR sparing priority input. The AI-predicted fluence maps are computationally efficient, making intuitive tradeoff tuning real-time. Further, this study demonstrates the promising performance of the AI system beyond traditional inverse planning loop and may potentially enhance AI's adoption in clinical planning process.

articles.title: Hidden Pitfalls of artificial intelligence in pediatric emergency radiology: a pictorial review of failure modes, clinical implications, and mitigation strategies.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming diagnostic radiology, yet its current clinical application in pediatric imaging remains fraught with challenges. Considerations that are unique to pediatric patients, including vast variations in developmental anatomy, age-specific disease patterns and pathologies, and technical variability create diagnostic challenges for which many commercially available AI systems, trained predominantly on adult data, are ill-equipped. This review utilizes literature evidence and illustrative clinical cases to critically examine various weaknesses of AI in pediatric imaging. Common pitfalls include misclassification of normal developmental variants, inability to distinguish pathological mimics, vulnerability to motion artifacts, modality-specific limitations, and errors introduced by artifacts or confounders. These failures are amplified by limited pediatric training data, annotation bias, and lack of contextual integration. We propose a structured framework for mitigating these risks, including pediatric-specific data curation, contextual model adaptation, algorithmic transparency, integrated feedback systems, technologist training, case-appropriate sedation planning, and centralized error tracking. These interventions are essential to enable safe, reliable, and ethically responsible AI deployment in pediatric emergency radiology.

articles.title: Identification of Vulnerable Plaques in Moderate-to-Severe Stenosis Using Texture Analysis Ultrasound Carotid Elastography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of texture features obtained from ultrasound strain elastography for detecting vulnerable carotid plaques with moderate-to-severe stenosis. METHODS: Eighty-eight moderate-to-severe stenosis patients, who underwent B-mode ultrasound, ultrasound elastography, then carotid endarterectomy, were included. Stable and vulnerable plaques were identified by Oil Red O and hematoxylin and eosin staining on post-surgery tissues. Four texture features, based on strain values in ultrasound elastography, were obtained: contrast, equality, non-correlation, and capacity. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis evaluated the predictive capabilities of B-mode ultrasound and ultrasound elastography for distinguishing between histologically-verified vulnerable versus stable plaques. RESULTS: Histopathological analyses identified 40 stable and 48 vulnerable plaques. Furthermore, ultrasound elastography was more sensitive and accurate for detecting vulnerable plaques, with sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 83.3, 70, and 77.3%, respectively, compared to B-mode ultrasound, which were 66.7, 72.5, and 69.3%. With respect to texture features, of the 4 assessed texture parameters, only contrast and non-correlation showed significant intergroup differences and were included in ROC analysis. However, contrast was the most accurate for vulnerable plaque identification, with an area under the curve of 0.81 (0.72-0.89), versus 0.69 (0.58-0.81) for non-correlation. Contrast also had higher maximum accuracy (77.3 versus 72.7%), sensitivity (83.3 versus 77.08%), and specificity (70.0 versus 67.5%) than non-correlation. CONCLUSION: Texture analysis ultrasound carotid elastography, particularly contrast, could serve as an additional diagnostic approach for classifying vulnerable plaques. This is owed to vulnerable plaques demonstrating greater deformation pattern complexity, which correlates to plaque tissue heterogeneity.

articles.title: Editorial for "Reversal of Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI-Assessed Left Atrial Fibrosis Following Cardioversion in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation".
Femoral Artery Compression Ultrasound as an Adjunct to Clinical ROSC Assessment During CPR: A Prospective Observational Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation requires rapid assessment of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), but manual pulse palpation is subjective and may be unreliable in low-flow states. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and diagnostic performance of femoral artery compression ultrasound (POCUS-FAC) as an adjunct to clinical ROSC assessment during CPR. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational feasibility study compared POCUS-FAC findings with clinician-adjudicated ROSC decisions in adult emergency department patients with non-traumatic cardiac arrest. POCUS-FAC included transverse femoral artery visualization, standardized compressibility assessment, and visible pulsation recording. Failure of the femoral artery to compress was defined as a positive compression finding. The resuscitation team leader, blinded to POCUS-FAC findings, made the ROSC decision using manual pulse palpation, monitor rhythm, clinical signs of circulation, respiratory effort, and measurable blood pressure when available. RESULTS: Of 57 evaluated patients, 52 were included. Clinician-adjudicated ROSC occurred in 24 patients, whereas 28 patients did not achieve ROSC. A total of 2196 POCUS-FAC and 549 manual palpation assessments were recorded. POCUS-FAC assessment time was shorter than manual palpation time (2.54 s versus 5.81 seconds; p < .001). Using clinician-adjudicated ROSC as the reference, POCUS-FAC compression positivity had 95.8% sensitivity and 89.3% specificity. Visible femoral artery pulsation occurred only in patients with clinician-adjudicated ROSC in this cohort. In 23 patients, compression positivity preceded manual pulse recognition; however, this finding should be interpreted in light of the more frequent POCUS-FAC sampling schedule. CONCLUSIONS: POCUS-FAC may be a rapid and feasible vascular ultrasound adjunct to clinical ROSC assessment during CPR. Before independent diagnostic use, it should be validated against objective hemodynamic measures such as invasive arterial pressure or Doppler-derived flow.

articles.title: Multiparametric MRI biomarkers of acute-to-chronic radiation-induced submandibular gland injury in a rat model.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess acute-to-chronic radiation-induced SMG injury using multiparametric MRI and investigate the histopathological correlates of quantitative MRI association. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty female Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to the Sham or irradiation (IR) group (n = 20 each). Bilateral SMGs in the IR group received a single 15-Gy dose of irradiation. Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) and T2 mapping MRI were performed before irradiation (baseline) and at one assigned terminal time point (24 h, day 7, week 8, and week 16 post-irradiation; n = 5 per group per time point). Histopathological analysis included acinar cell area percentage (AC%), aquaporin 5 (AQP5) positive area fraction, Ki-67 proliferation index, microvessel density (MVD) and fibrosis. Two-way ANOVA was used to assess group and time effects, and Spearman correlation was applied for MRI-histopathological associations. RESULTS: Compared with time-matched sham controls, D was lower at 24 h (P = 0.041), not significantly different at day 7, and higher at weeks 8 (P = 0.016) and 16 (P < 0.0001); T2 was elevated throughout (all P < 0.0001); The f value was significantly higher at 24 h, day 7, and week 8 (all P < 0.001), whereas fD* was significantly higher only at 24 h (P < 0.05); AQP5 and Ki-67 were reduced and MVD increased at all time points; AC% decreased and fibrosis increased at weeks 8 and 16. Pooled Spearman correlations (n = 40) associated D with AC% (r = -0.590) and AQP5 (r = -0.430), T2 with AC% (r = 0.573), and f (r = 0.807) and fD* (r = 0.568) with MVD (all Holm-adjusted P ≤ 0.012); D* was not associated with MVD (P = 0.514). CONCLUSIONS: IVIM- and T2-derived parameters may serve as potential imaging markers for assessing acute-to-chronic radiation-induced SMG injury.

articles.title: Lateral, dorsoventral and anterioposterior shifts in resting state functional connectivity after GABAA receptor agonistic and antagonistic treatment in the rat brain.
articles.abstract: GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the mammalian brain. In the present study, we assessed functional connectivity (rs-FC) in the rat brain after challenge with the GABAA receptor (R) agonist and antagonist muscimol (MUS) and bicuculline (BIC), respectively. Rs-fMRI measurements were performed on 12 male Wistar rats anaesthetized with a mixture of ketamine (0.45 mg/kg) and xylazine (0.2 mg/kg) in baseline (BAS) and after intraperitoneal injection of MUS (1 mg/kg) and BIC (1 mg/kg). Data were analyzed with both independent component and neural traffic (NT) analysis. Comparisons to BAS as well as between agonistic and antagonistic treatment evidenced that activations and deactivations in neocortex, basal ganglia, thalamic nuclei, limbic system and brain stem, along with voxel-wise increases and decreases of NT, shifted between sides or between portions of individual regions in dorsoventral and/or anterioposterior direction. The appearance or disappearance of activations in a specific brain region may be interpreted to reflect, at least in part, elevated and reduced direct GABAAR agonistic and antagonistic action, respectively, in the afferent and efferent connections of the region in question. Apart from the actual synaptic flow of inhibitory neurotransmitter, however, the increase or decrease of NT relative to BAS also reflects the concomitant effects of those neurotransmitters subject to inhibitory GABAergic action. Thereby, the initial point of BAS as well as challenge is the neurochemical condition exerted by the N-methyl d-aspartate receptor antagonistic and α2 adrenoreceptor agonistic action of ketamine and xylazine, respectively.

articles.title: Computed tomography in the trauma emergency department and its association with length of stay.
articles.abstract: AIM: Prolonged emergency department length of stay (ED-LOS) is associated with adverse outcomes and operational inefficiency. Computed tomography (CT) is central to trauma evaluation, but reporting delays may contribute to prolonged ED-LOS. This study assessed the association between CT report turnaround time (RTAT) and ED-LOS among trauma patients in a high-volume, resource-limited emergency department. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including adult trauma patients admitted to a tertiary academic hospital in South Africa between January and March 2022. Demographic, clinical, and imaging timestamp data were extracted. Computed tomography time (CTT), provisional report turnaround time (PRTAT), and final report turnaround time (FRTAT) were calculated. Associations with ED-LOS were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusting for age, sex, Shock Index, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), and CTT. RESULTS: A total of 1,246 patients were included (mean age: 33.9 ± 11.9 years; 87.6% male), of whom 729 (58.5%) underwent CT imaging. Mean ED-LOS was 8.9 ± 5.7 hours and was significantly longer in CT than in non-CT patients (10.7 vs 6.3 hours; P < .001). Median CTT was 5.1 hours (interquartile range [IQR]: 3.0-8.3), PRTAT was 2.1 hours (IQR: 1.3-3.6), and FRTAT was 11.2 hours (IQR: 6.1-17.2). In multivariable analysis, only PRTAT remained independently associated with ED-LOS (β = 0.33 hours per 1-hour increase; 95% CI: 0.04-0.62; P = .026). CONCLUSION: CT utilisation and radiology workflow intervals were associated with prolonged ED-LOS in trauma patients. Radiology reporting workflows may represent a potential target for improving patient flow in resource-limited emergency settings.

articles.title: Benign histopathologic spectrum of concordant human-artificial intelligence false-positive mammographic findings.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the benign histopathologic spectrum of mammographic findings independently considered suspicious by radiologists and artificial intelligence (AI) and explore differences according to mammographic presentation. METHODS: This retrospective two-center study included women who underwent screening or diagnostic mammography in 2025. Eligible lesions were classified as BI-RADS category 4 or 5 by radiologists blinded to AI output, had a localized AI score of at least 20 at the same location, and showed benign histopathology after biopsy. Individual histopathologic comparisons used two-sided Fisher's exact tests with Holm adjustment across seven comparisons. RESULTS: The cohort included 91 women (mean age, 56.4 ± 9.8 years). Findings comprised 61 calcifications (67.0%), 28 mass-category findings (30.8%), and two combined findings (2.2%). Benign breast changes were the most frequent histopathologic group (47/91, 51.6%). Excluding combined findings, distributions differed between calcifications and mass-category findings (p < 0.001). Benign breast changes were more frequent among calcifications (39/61 [63.9%] vs 8/28 [28.6%]; p = 0.019), whereas fibroepithelial tumors were more frequent among mass-category findings (8/28 [28.6%] vs 4/61 [6.6%]; p = 0.048). CONCLUSION: Among concordant radiologist-AI false-positive findings, calcifications were the most frequent mammographic presentation and were predominantly associated with benign breast changes, whereas mass-category findings were relatively enriched for fibroepithelial tumors. These exploratory findings may improve awareness of benign mimickers that trigger concordant human-AI suspicion.

articles.title: Topographic Anatomy of Perithyroidal Fascial Spaces: In Vivo Sonographic Mapping of Morphology and Hydrodynamics.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterize the in vivo sonographic morphology and fluid dynamics of perithyroidal fascial spaces during hydrodissection and to assess their relevance to ultrasound-guided thyroid interventions. METHODS: This prospective study evaluated 24 participants (30 target nodules or lobes) undergoing ultrasound-guided thyroid thermal ablation. After saline hydrodissection, the anterior cervical, visceral, and post-thyroid spaces were assessed using a 3-tier sonographic classification: type I (anechoic), type II (stranded), and type III (mixed). The visceral space was stratified into upper pole, mid-portion, and lower pole levels. Fluid distribution, anatomical boundaries, and intrafascial contents were tracked in real time. RESULTS: Sonographic morphology varied across the perithyroidal spaces. The anterior cervical space was predominantly type I (23 of 24, 95.8%), whereas the post-thyroid space was mainly type II (18 of 24, 75.0%) and revealed traversing vascular structures. Type III morphology was observed in 9 of 15 mid-portion visceral-space assessments (60.0%) and was not observed in the assessed upper- or lower-pole regions. In the visceral space, post-injection fluid distribution differed according to the injection location relative to the ligament of Berry. Thyroid vascular roots and a structure sonographically consistent with a parathyroid gland were visualized within polar confluence regions. CONCLUSIONS: Hydrodissection can serve as a real-time sonographic mapping tool for perithyroidal fascial spaces. These findings provide an in vivo sonographic framework for understanding perithyroidal fascial anatomy and may inform anatomical assessment during ultrasound-guided thyroid ablation.
